title: autotrade (주식/키움) — 005930 1m cycle
_why: The stock side. Crypto has its own file (pipeline.upbit.example.json) because almost
everything differs: the broker, the hours, the timeframe and the fee. Sharing one file
meant a coin ran on a weekday-daytime cron against a broker with no crypto.
One cycle, wired the only way the layers allow: this module never calls a broker, the
pipeline does. Steps are 0-based, so $step0 is the gate and $step2 is the candle fetch.
The gate comes first so that a switched-off day ends here, before any broker call — the
CONDITION exits the run cleanly rather than failing it, which is what keeps the cron log
readable when trading is off for a week. It also reports the trade, so this file names no
symbol, account or timeframe of its own: changing any of them is a settings edit.
The candle call asks for an interval rather than an API id — minute bars, daily, weekly and
monthly are four different endpoints at this broker, and a strategy that changes timeframe
must not require editing the call.
Scheduled runs carry the cron context, so the order step needs no approval card — that is
the whole reason trading lives here and not in chat.
The three queries at the end are reads and are not approval-gated; reconcile settles from
them in the order fills -> open orders -> balance.

_note: The pipeline does nothing until a strategy is declared in the module settings —
`cycle` answers 'no enabled strategy matched'. Paste one entry like this into the
`strategies` field (전략 탭). `account` is the broker module's account alias, and that
alias is what decides mock vs real — mode=dryrun still places no orders at all.
